    Splitting the regular part of a linear relation #

    Let R ⊆ X × X be a linear relation on a finite-dimensional space and N ≤ X a subspace in which every vector has an R-successor and an R-predecessor. Let K ≤ N consist of the vectors of N with a chain in N to 0 (Kinf). Then K is closed under successors (fwd_mem), and N = U ⊕ K for a subspace U on which R restricts to the graph of an automorphism (exists_split).

    The proof chooses a section of R that is nilpotent on K (it lowers the length of the chain to 0) and solves a Sylvester equation by a finite Neumann series.
